double-underline.context: A capital letter A with two parallel lines beneath it. Used in text editors for the double underline format and for accounting style totals.

dotted-underline.context: A capital letter A with a row of evenly spaced dots beneath it. Used for the dotted underline text format, link hints and glossary terms.

dashed-underline.context: A capital letter A with a dashed line beneath it. Used for the dashed underline text format and spelling or grammar marks.

overline.context: A capital letter A with a single bar above its apex. Used for the overline text format, overbar notation and negation marks.

double-strikethrough.context: A letter S crossed by two close parallel lines. Used for the double strikethrough text format when marking removed or cancelled text.

bold-italic.context: A heavy slanted capital B with thick strokes leaning right. Used for the combined bold and italic text format in editors.

embossed-text.context: A capital letter A with a shadow edge offset to its lower right so it looks raised from the page. Used for emboss and bevel text effects in design software.

glowing-text.context: A capital letter A surrounded by short rays as if it shines. Used for glow and neon text effects in design tools and video titles.

gradient-text.context: A bold capital letter A whose strokes fade from solid on the left to dashes on the right. Used for gradient fill and fade text effects.

extruded-text.context: A capital letter A with depth lines running back from its corners like a block letter in three dimensions. Used for extrude and 3D text effects.

reflected-text.context: A capital letter A standing on a line with a broken upside-down copy beneath. Used for reflection and mirror text effects.

knockout-text.context: A solid rounded square with the letter A cut out of it so the background shows through. Used for knockout, reversed and masked text effects.

warped-text.context: A letter A inside a lens-shaped envelope bounded by two curved guide lines. Used for warp, arc and envelope distort text tools.

sketched-text.context: A capital letter A drawn with loose crossing strokes that overshoot at the ends. Used for hand drawn, pencil and sketch text styles.

distressed-text.context: A bold capital letter A with gaps and specks worn out of its strokes. Used for grunge, vintage and distressed text textures.

glitch-text.context: A capital letter A sliced into three bands with the middle band shifted sideways. Used for glitch, distortion and digital error text effects.

perspective-text.context: A receding page of ruled text lines that narrows toward the top. Used for perspective and 3D tilt text transforms, like a title crawl.

camel-case.context: The letters a, B and c with a hump arc over the raised capital in the middle. Used for camelCase naming convention in programming and code style settings.

snake-case.context: The letters a and b joined by a low line at the baseline. Used for the snake case naming convention in code, filenames and database fields.

kebab-case.context: The letters a and b joined by a short hyphen at mid height. Used for kebab-case naming in urls, css classes and filenames.

raised-initial.context: A large capital A sitting on the first line of text and rising above the text block. Used for raised cap and initial letter paragraph styles.

text-expansion.context: The letter A followed by a dot, an arrow and a longer block of text. Used for text expander, snippet and abbreviation shortcut tools.

paraphrase.context: Two text lines with a pair of circular arrows between them. Used for paraphrasing, rewording and rewrite tools in writing assistants.

expand-text.context: A short text line that opens out into three longer lines. Used for expanding or lengthening text in writing and summarising tools.

writers-block.context: A pen nib pressed against a small brick wall. Used for writer's block, creative blocks and stuck-in-writing states.

pen-name.context: A quill pen crossing in front of a small domino eye mask. Used for pen names, pseudonyms and anonymous author features.

style-manual.context: A closed book with a large letter A on its cover and a bookmark ribbon. Used for style guides, brand books and editorial handbooks.

variable-font.context: A capital letter A above a horizontal slider with a round knob. Used for variable fonts and adjustable weight or width axes.

font-width.context: A capital letter A with horizontal arrows pointing outward from both sides. Used for font width, stretch, condensed and expanded settings.

optical-size.context: A small bold letter A beside a large thin letter A on a shared baseline. Used for the optical size axis, which adjusts a typeface to its display size.

font-interpolation.context: Three vertical stems growing from thin to heavy above a line with end and middle points. Used for weight interpolation between font masters in type design tools.

pixel-font.context: A capital letter A built from square pixel blocks on a stepped grid. Used for pixel, bitmap and retro game fonts.

geometric-sans-font.context: A lowercase a formed by a perfect circle with a straight vertical stem. Used for geometric sans serif typefaces and modernist type styles.

handwritten-font.context: Loose handwritten letters A and a with a flowing underline swoosh. Used for handwriting, script and casual hand lettered font categories.

dingbat-font.context: A grid of four small symbols: a star, a heart, a check mark and scissors. Used for dingbat, symbol and ornament fonts.

icon-font.context: A tall glyph cell with a baseline guide holding a small house symbol instead of a letter. Used for icon fonts and symbol glyph sets.

font-fallback.context: A dashed outline letter A with an arrow pointing to a solid letter A. Used for font fallback, font stacks and substitute typefaces.

embedded-font.context: A document page with a square badge holding the letter A on its lower right. Used for fonts embedded in documents and pdf files.

missing-glyph.context: A tall empty rectangle crossed by an X, the placeholder box for a character a font lacks. Used for missing glyph, tofu and unsupported character states.

font-hinting.context: A grid of cells with squares filled in the pattern of a capital A. Used for font hinting, pixel snapping and screen rendering settings.

hand-lettering.context: A brush pen drawing a swooping stroke that runs from thick to thin. Used for hand lettering, brush calligraphy and lettering art.

swash-letter.context: A capital letter A whose right leg sweeps into a long flourish beneath the baseline. Used for swash capitals, flourishes and ornamental alternates.

stylistic-alternates.context: A double-storey lowercase a and a single-storey lowercase a with a swap arrow between. Used for stylistic alternates and stylistic sets in font features.

old-style-figures.context: The digits 1, 3 and 4 with the 3 and 4 dropping below the baseline. Used for old style figures, text numerals and the onum font feature.

tabular-figures.context: Two rows of digits lined up in equal-width columns. Used for tabular figures, monospaced digits and aligned number columns in tables and prices.

slashed-zero.context: A tall rounded zero with a diagonal slash through its centre. Used for the slashed zero font feature and code fonts that separate zero from the letter O.

discretionary-ligature.context: The letters s and t joined at the top by a curved arc. Used for discretionary, decorative and historical ligatures in font features.

full-width-character.context: A narrow letter A beside a wide letter A inside a square cell. Used for full width characters, zenkaku forms and double width cjk text.

letter-ascender.context: A lowercase h with the part of its stem above the x height drawn heavy. Used to teach ascenders in type anatomy and font metrics.
keywords: b d f h k l

letter-descender.context: A lowercase p with the part of its stem below the baseline drawn heavy. Used to teach descenders in type anatomy and line spacing.

cap-height.context: A capital H beside two guide ticks and a vertical arrow measuring its height. Used for cap height in font metrics and type measurement.

tittle.context: A lowercase i with its dot circled by a small ring. Used to name the tittle, the dot over an i or j, in type anatomy.

letter-crossbar.context: A capital A outline with only its crossbar drawn heavy. Used to teach the crossbar in type anatomy.

letter-apex.context: A capital A with a small circle marking the pointed top where its strokes meet. Used to teach the apex in type anatomy.

letter-vertex.context: A capital V with a small circle marking the pointed bottom where its strokes meet. Used to teach the vertex in type anatomy.

letter-bowl.context: A lowercase b with its rounded bowl drawn heavy and its stem light. Used to teach the bowl in type anatomy.

letter-counter.context: A capital O outline with the enclosed inner space filled solid. Used to teach the counter, the empty space inside a letter, in type anatomy.

letter-ear.context: A double-storey lowercase g with a small flag at its upper right circled. Used to teach the ear in type anatomy.

letter-spine.context: A capital S with its central diagonal stroke drawn heavy and its ends light. Used to teach the spine of an S in type anatomy.

letter-tail.context: A capital Q with the short tail stroke across its bottom drawn heavy. Used to teach the tail of a Q in type anatomy.

letter-terminal.context: A lowercase c with the end of its upper arm circled. Used to teach terminals, the ends of strokes, in type anatomy.

letter-spur.context: A capital G with the small projection at its lower right circled. Used to teach the spur in type anatomy.

letter-stem.context: A lowercase l with its main vertical stroke drawn heavy and a light curved foot. Used to teach the stem in type anatomy.

letter-shoulder.context: A lowercase n with the arched curve that springs from its stem drawn heavy. Used to teach the shoulder in type anatomy.

letter-arm.context: A capital E with its top horizontal stroke drawn heavy. Used to teach the arm in type anatomy.

letter-leg.context: A capital R with its diagonal lower stroke drawn heavy. Used to teach the leg in type anatomy.

letter-loop.context: A double-storey lowercase g with its closed lower loop drawn heavy. Used to teach the loop in type anatomy.

letter-overshoot.context: A round letter O rising above and dipping below a flat H beside it. Used to explain overshoot, the optical correction for round letters.

stroke-contrast.context: A letter O with thick sides and thin top and bottom. Used to show stroke contrast, the thick to thin variation within letters.

stress-axis.context: A letter O with uneven stroke weight and a tilted dashed line through its thinnest points. Used to show the stress axis of a typeface.

ink-trap.context: A thick corner junction of two strokes with a small wedge notch cut into the inside corner. Used to explain ink traps in type design.

em-square.context: A square frame holding a letter A that stands on a baseline guide. Used for the em square, the design box of a glyph, in font metrics.

advance-width.context: A letter n between two side ticks with a dimension arrow spanning the full width below. Used for advance width and sidebearings in font metrics.

vertical-metrics.context: A capital H and a lowercase p beside a ruler with four ticks for cap height, x height, baseline and descender. Used for vertical font metrics and line height.

word-spacing.context: Two word blocks on a line with a two-headed arrow in the gap between them. Used for word spacing and interword gap settings.

baseline-shift.context: A capital A beside a smaller raised letter a with a short up arrow beneath it. Used for baseline shift, raised or lowered text and vertical offset.

hanging-punctuation.context: Left-aligned text lines with an opening quotation mark sitting outside the left edge. Used for hanging punctuation and optical margin alignment.

first-line-indent.context: A paragraph whose first line starts further in, marked by a small arrow. Used for first line indent and paragraph indentation settings.

hanging-indent.context: A paragraph with the first line flush left and the lines below it indented. Used for hanging indents in bibliographies, citations and lists.

non-breaking-space.context: The letters a and b joined by a small upturned arc bridging the space between them. Used for the non-breaking space character that keeps words on one line.
